# Answer: every module of 725 PyPI projects imported on the restricted Pyodide core

For window-ml's python-packages lane (laptop session 19f583d1). The request and the scripts are in
`inbox/ui-api/pkg-imports/`. Run on mlbox on 2026-11-12, approved by Shane in this session the same day.
The data is in `pkg-imports/`: `summary.jsonl` is the driver's output, one row per project, and
`raw.tar.gz` holds `raw/<project>.jsonl` for all 725.

**The one crash is `pillow==12.2.0`.** It took Pyodide down while importing `PIL._imagingtk`, after 93
modules had imported. The row's `stderr_tail` holds only the last 400 characters of the stack, so I reran
that one project alone to get the cause:

```
Pyodide has suffered a fatal error. Please report this to the Pyodide maintainers.
The cause of the fatal error was:
RuntimeError: function signature mismatch
```

This is a wasm trap, not a Python exception, so it takes the whole interpreter down, and with it every
module after `_imagingtk` in the ordered list. Those modules were never tried.

**One import tried to reach the network.** The proxy refused a single `CONNECT huggingface.co:443` at
14:29:51Z. With 12 workers running, I can't tell which project it came from. Every other connection went to
the three allowed hosts: 554 to `pypi.org`, 554 to `files.pythonhosted.org` and 140 to
`cdn.jsdelivr.net`. Outside the proxy there was no network at all.

## The run

| | |
|---|---|
| wall time | 2 min 24 s (14:29:29Z to 14:31:53Z), all 725 projects in a single pass |
| workers, timeout | 12, 900 s per project. Nothing came close: the slowest took 24.2 s |
| image | `node:26-bookworm` (`sha256:b7087bc4d973…`): Node v26.13.1, Python 3.11.2 for the driver |
| Pyodide | 314.0.3, CPython 3.14.2 restricted-mode, from window-ml `7d7d1b1f` via `npm run fetch-pyodide` |
| pins | `pins.txt` sha256 `e140dd65…ff30`, as sent |
| limits | `--cpus 16 --memory 64g --pids-limit 4096`, `--cap-drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, uid 1000, no GPUs, no credentials |

**How the network was limited.** The container ran on a Docker `--internal` network, which has no route
out. It could reach one other container, a 30-line allowlist CONNECT proxy. That proxy accepted only
`CONNECT <host>:443` and only for the listed hosts, and it logged every request. The container was pointed
at it with `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`. Node 26's fetch honours that, and so do micropip's
downloads. The setup ran first, with its own allowlist: github.com, registry.npmjs.org, cdn.jsdelivr.net and
release-assets.githubusercontent.com. The probe then ran with only `pypi.org`,
`files.pythonhosted.org` and `cdn.jsdelivr.net`. Before either phase, a check confirmed that a direct
connect failed and that example.com got a 403 from the proxy.

**Mounts.** The clone lived in a Docker volume that only the setup and probe containers used. The only host
directory mounted into the probe was the output directory. The scripts were copied into the volume
beforehand rather than mounted.

## Changes to your scripts

None. `probe-all.mjs`, `drive.py` and `pins.txt` ran exactly as sent. The setup steps also worked
unchanged on Linux. The only fix was making the new volume writable by uid 1000, which is a Docker detail.

Three things to know when reading the data:

- **A crash row's `stderr_tail` loses the cause.** `drive.py` keeps the last 400 characters, and for a wasm
  trap that is all stack frames. Keeping the head as well would have caught "function signature mismatch".
- **`datadog-api-client` hit `MAX_MODULES` (5000), so its row is truncated.** The modules beyond the cap
  were never tried.
- **Python projects only.** This tests imports on your restricted build. It does not test functionality.
  Whether a ModuleNotFoundError is a real gap or an optional extra (for example, pydantic-ai's
  "install huggingface_hub") is for you to sort out from the raw rows.

Clean-up: the run, proxy and setup containers, the internal network and the clone volume were removed
afterwards. The outputs also remain on the box in `/srv/fast/pkgprobe/out/`.

## Follow-up: what reached for huggingface.co (2026-11-12, 14:36Z)

The python-packages lane asked me to rerun huggingface-hub on its own, with 1 worker, in the same sandbox,
then safetensors if that didn't reproduce it. This time both the proxy and the probe's stdout were
timestamped to the millisecond. The files are `pkg-imports/rerun-proxy.log` and
`pkg-imports/rerun-huggingface-hub.ts.jsonl`.

**It reproduced on the first try, and the import responsible is `import huggingface_hub.cli`
(huggingface-hub 2.4.0).**

```
14:36:10.304 {"ev": "start", "m": "huggingface_hub.cli"}
14:36:10.362 CONNECT huggingface.co:443 DENY                 (proxy log)
14:36:10.365 {"ev": "import", "m": "huggingface_hub.cli", "ok": true, "s": 0.061}
```

The import **succeeded** in 61 ms and did not wait on the refusal. The connection must have started in the
background or not been awaited. It was the only connection to huggingface.co in the whole run. safetensors
was rerun afterwards anyway (8 modules), and it made no connection outside the allowlist. The project
took 8.3 s on its own, against 12.0 s with 12 workers. No single import is slow: the slowest is
`_bucket_live_follow` at 0.27 s.

Reading the wheel, I could not find where the call is made. `cli/__init__.py` imports only `cli._output`,
which builds an `Output()` object when it loads. Nothing there calls the network directly, so the call is
further down that import chain. I stopped at that point.
